name: Kathryn Lueders
title: Associate Administrator for Human Exploration and Operations Mission Directorate at NASA
bio: Kathryn Lueders is the NASA Associate Administrator of the Human Exploration and Operations Mission Directorate. Kathryn began her NASA career in 1992 at the White Sands Test Facility in New Mexico, where she was the Shuttle Orbital Maneuvering System and Reaction Control Systems Depot manager. She later moved to the International Space Station Program and served as transportation integration manager, where she led commercial cargo resupply services to the space station. Prior to becoming Associate Administrator, Kathryn served as the Program Manager for the Commercial Crew Program for seven years, where she directed NASA's efforts to send astronauts to space on private spacecraft, culminating in the successful launch of Demo-2 from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida on May 30, 2020. She holds a Bachelor of Business Administration in Finance from the University of New Mexico, and a Bachelor of Science and Master of Science in Industrial Engineering from New Mexico State University.

name: Adia Gooden, Ph.D.
title: Director of the Clinic and Community Programs at The Family Institute
bio: Dr. Adia Gooden is a licensed clinical psychologist, dynamic speaker and trainer, who is passionate about cultivating unconditional self-worth in others. Dr. Adia currently serves as the Director of the Clinic and Community Programs at The Family Institute at Northwestern University, where she has an active clinical practice and treats individuals and couples. She has spent more than a decade working with clients to embody mental wellness in their everyday lives and to engage boldly with the world. Dr. Adia received her bachelor's degree from Stanford University and earned her PhD in Clinical Community Psychology from DePaul University. She served as a Staff Psychologist and the Coordinator for Multicultural Outreach and Support at The University of Chicago Student Counseling Service for four years.

name: Lana Potts
title: Indigenous Health and First Nation Expert, Medical Doctor
bio: Dr. Lana Rose Potts MD CCFP “Last To Come In” is a Family Physician who specializes in First Nation Health. She provides primary care at the Siksika Health and Wellness Centre and is the Medical Director for the Piikani Nation. Dr. Potts is a charter class graduate of The Northern Ontario School of Medicine in Thunder Bay, Ontario. Lana completed her residency training in Indigenous Family Medicine at UBC. She has also completed a Bachelor of Science in Nursing with Distinction at the University of Alberta. Lana is a member of the Piikani Nation. She was fortunate to be raised in ceremony and receive influence and teachings from her late mother Hazel Potts, grandmother Rose Potts and other matriarchs in Blackfoot Territory. She is married to Robert Benjoe from Muscowpetung First Nation in Saskatchewan and is the proud mother to her daughter Annataki and son Nodin. Dr. Potts' advocates in many ways on behalf of Indigenous and rural health. Lana is a self proclaimed Indigenous child health advocate. Her medical practice philosophy is taking her Blackfoot teachings and mending them with western medicine. She is also a renowned speaker on various Indigenous Health issues and a member of the Canada Speakers Bureau.

name: Ambre Lizurey
title: Director of Operations at EA's Motive Montreal studio
bio: After graduating in Business Administration at HEC Montréal, Ambre studied cognitive ergonomics at Polytechnique Montréal. She cumulates more than 12 years of experience in the video game industry, which she acquired in major studios. First, at Ubisoft where she joined the production team working on the Assassin's Creed brand, and then at Reflector Entertainment as Head of Operations. Ambre is now Director of Operations at EA's Motive Montreal studio in charge of developing the game studio and reinforcing the projects' structure standards. In parallel, Ambre volunteers to help the STEM industries be more diverse, by showing young girls the possibilities available in the field.
